To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) mitochondrial fusion and fissions regulate mitochondrial network expansion and maturation, 2) the mitochondrial network is a key regulator of the energetic continuum, and 3) mitochondrial oxidative metabolism is required to support the differentiation and maturation of stem cells into functional cardiomyocytes.
mitochondrial oxidative metabolism is required to support the differentiation of stem and progenitor cells into energetically and contractile competent cardiomyocytes.

the energetic requirements for stem cell differentiation are defined by mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, which must be programmed to support cardiac specification and excite contraction coupling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of mitochondria in cardiac development.
the metabolic mechanisms that underlie cardiac specification and excitable function.
the role of mitochondria in the differentiation of embryonic cells into a cardiac phenotype.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mitochondrial oxidative metabolism is required to support the differentiation of embryonic cells into cardiomyocytes.
the energetic switch from anaerobic to oxidative metabolism is required to secure cardiac specification, sarcomere assembly, and excitation contraction function.
Mitochondrial oxidative metabolism, rather than glycolytic metabolism is required to support the cardiac specification of embryonic stem cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mitochondrial system is a critical regulator of stem cell differentiation into a functional cardiac cell.
the mitochondrial system is a critical regulator of cardiac specification.

the metabolic reprogramming required for cardiac differentiation of embryonal stem cells is dependent upon the formation of the mitochondrial network and the subsequent engagement of oxidative metabolism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mitochondrial metabolism is required for stem cell differentiation.
the energetic requirements of stem cells must be met to ensure the specification of a functional cardiac phenotype.
mitochondrial bioenergetics and the metabolic micro-environment are critical regulators of de-novo cardiogenesis and targets of heart regeneration.
